rationale: Re-review after fixes. CR-002 (null assistant_ids guarded with `or []` in streaming.py), CR-003 (test_strip_response_keeps_only_reduced_interrupted_thoughts) and CR-004 (workflow-exemption tests in test_tool_output_visibility.py and routers/test_conversation.py) are resolved in f83d60a41. 2fcb76f0a stops tool error text leaking through hidden-output streams and 5f8eade8f leaves a single Alembic head. CR-001 (resume ignores a version-pinned hide decision) is an accepted, documented gap: it is stated as KNOWN GAP in the _ask_assistant_resume docstring and needs a pinned version with hide ON and the master flag OFF. It is not fixed by this MR.

standards_review.notes: All authored commit subjects in the range use the EPMCDME-15555: Description format; the only exceptions are auto-generated 'Merge branch' commits, which the squash-merge default replaces

New concern placed in its own module tool_output_visibility.py (210 lines) rather than appended to large files; additions to the 1000+ line models are 1-3 lines; license headers present on all new .py files
No credential logging, auth bypass or lossy input parsing seen; the only logger call logs the response type name; changes strip tool outputs fail-closed on egress paths

findings.title: Resume ignores version-pinned hide decision
findings.problem: _ask_assistant_resume applies only the master assistant's hide_tool_outputs flag. ToolCallResumeRequest has no version and resume skips _prepare_assistant_for_execution, so a turn paused under a pinned version that hides outputs is resumed unhidden if the master flag is off. The docstring calls this a KNOWN GAP and marks it out of scope with no ticket.
findings.impact: Resumed turn streams full tool outputs that the pinned version was configured to hide, the same bypass _effective_hide_tool_outputs closes on the other ask paths. Reachability not fully confirmed (needs pinned version with hide on and master off).
findings.recommendation: Persist the effective hide decision (or pinned version) in the checkpoint when the tool call is paused and apply it on resume; otherwise link a tracked ticket and add a test pinning the current behavior.
findings.resolution: accepted-gap: documented as KNOWN GAP in execution.py:269; not fixed in this MR

findings.title: Null assistant_ids breaks live stream
findings.problem: conversation.assistant_ids + [conversation.initial_assistant_id] raises TypeError when assistant_ids is None; the column is Optional[List[str]] (models/conversation.py:263).
findings.impact: The live conversation stream endpoint returns 500 for a non-workflow conversation with a NULL assistant_ids. Reachability unconfirmed: the default is an empty list, so only legacy or null rows are affected.

findings.title: No test for strip_response interrupted thoughts
findings.problem: The non-stream path (strip_response / apply_to_response on BaseModelResponse) with an interrupted thought is untested. test_apply_to_response_sync_base_model_response uses a non-interrupted Thought; interrupted tests cover only strip_chunk and strip_history.
findings.impact: Reverting thoughts to [] (dropping the Allow/Deny approval thought) or leaking metadata/children on ask and resume responses would pass every test.
findings.recommendation: Add a test calling strip_response with BaseModelResponse(thoughts=[Thought(id='p', interrupted=True, input_text='{}', metadata={'x':1}), Thought(id='plain')]) asserting only the reduced interrupted thought remains.

findings.title: Workflow exemption guard untested
findings.problem: The is_workflow_conversation exemption in strip_history_for_conversation and in get_conversation_stream has no test; all hide_tool_outputs fixtures use plain non-workflow Conversations.
findings.impact: Removing either guard (which would feed WorkflowConfig ids into the assistant lookup or strip workflow output) passes every test.
findings.recommendation: Add tests with Conversation(is_workflow_conversation=True) and a lookup flagging its ids hidden, asserting history is untouched and the stream is not wrapped by strip_stream.
